saints.name: St. Francis Borgia
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: A Spanish duke who, shaken by the sight of a dead empress's ruined beauty, left his rank to become a Jesuit…
biography: Born in 1510 into one of the most powerful families of Spain, Francis Borgia was Duke of Gandía and a courtier of the Emperor Charles V. Charged with escorting the body of the Empress Isabella to burial, he is said to have been so struck by the corruption of her once-celebrated beauty that he resolved to serve only a Sovereign who could never die.

After the death of his wife he entered the Society of Jesus, renouncing his titles, and rose to become the order's third Superior General. Under his guidance the young society expanded across Europe and into the missions of the New World; he died in Rome in 1572 and is often called a “second founder” of the Jesuits.
saints.knownFor: Renouncing a dukedom to serve as a Jesuit.
